Sound studio

A low paddle hum, a midrange puck tone, and short, high wall cues keep each role distinct. Headphones give left-right position. These are stereo cues, not exact physical distances.

Adjust each layer, then audition it. Settings save on this device. Set a layer to zero to mute it. Changes affect the next game.

Listening for the walls

When your paddle enters the outer 18 percent of the screen, soft pulses sound in that ear. Pulses come faster as your paddle gets closer to the edge. Adjust the warning range above. A brief high tap also marks the puck hitting a wall. The continuous puck tone still gives the puck’s own left-right position.

How the game works

You defend the near end of the table. The computer defends the far end. Score by sending the puck past the computer’s paddle; the computer scores if the puck passes yours. First to seven goals wins.

Sliding your paddle

  1. Start the game, then place one finger on the play area below the score and buttons.
  2. Your finger’s horizontal position sets your paddle’s position: left side is left, middle is center, right side is right. Touching a new spot moves the paddle there immediately.
  3. Keep your finger on the screen and slide left or right to follow the puck’s sound. Moving up or down has no effect.
  4. Line up your paddle with the puck before it reaches your end. The hit happens automatically. You do not tap the puck, flick it forward, or swipe upward to shoot.
  5. Faster swipes do not make a harder shot. Hitting near the paddle’s center sends the puck more straight ahead; hitting near its edge adds sideways movement. The puck speeds up during rallies.
  6. If you lift your finger, the paddle stays where you left it. Touching down again sets it to that new horizontal position.

Example rally

If the puck is mostly in your left ear and its pitch is rising, it is approaching your left side. Slide left and line up the low paddle hum with the puck. A mellow knock means you returned it. As it travels away, its pitch and volume fall. Keep listening, because it may bounce off a side wall and change direction.

What each sound means

  • Puck: a midrange tone panned left or right. By default, higher and louder means closer to your goal; lower and quieter means farther away. You can change this approach cue in Sound studio. Pitch tells you distance, not speed.
  • Your paddle: a quiet, low hum. Its left-right position follows your finger.
  • Your hit: a mellow knock by default. Choose a light chime or soft note in Sound studio.
  • Computer’s hit: a shorter, slightly higher note.
  • Side wall: a brief high tap on the side the puck hit. Soft repeating pulses warn when your paddle is near a side wall.
  • Serve: three beeps before play begins.
  • You score: rising notes. The computer scores: falling notes. The updated score is spoken.

Before you start

Use stereo headphones with the left and right sides correctly placed. Sit with the phone steady. Keep your finger below the top controls. After the spoken introduction, the serve beeps begin. After each goal there is a brief pause, then another serve.

VoiceOver and pausing

With VoiceOver on, activate Start game. Then turn VoiceOver off for direct touch play; ordinary VoiceOver swipes navigate items instead of positioning your paddle. Turn it back on when you need the menu. You can use the side-button Accessibility Shortcut if configured. Switching away from the app pauses play. Use Resume to continue, or End game to return to this guide and reset the match.

Keyboard: Left and Right arrows move your paddle. Space pauses or resumes.

About this web version

Scoring rules and touch-position controls come from the GitHub game. The new sound system uses separate pitch bands, softer notes, individual volume controls and paddle edge warnings. This version adds a start menu, pause controls, browser speech and home-screen installation. The spoken voice can differ from Expo. Native iPhone vibration is unavailable. The GitHub gameplay screen is text on a black background; it does not include a drawn rink or moving puck.

Install on iPhone

Open this page in Safari. Choose Share, then Add to Home Screen. Leave Open as Web App enabled if shown, then choose Add.

Browser test version · Audio and touch supported. Native vibration is unavailable on iPhone web apps.
